nom: Lecture 1 — The UK: Birth of England & Great Britain
cartes: First mention of the Celts by Greek authors
Celts arrive on the shores of Britain (Iron Age)
Vikings found the city of Dublin (Ireland)
Boudicca, queen of the Iceni tribe, leads a revolt against Roman rule
Anglo-Saxons raid English shores and are beaten back by the Romans
Romans leave England, its shores are left unprotected
Arrival of the Jutes (from Jutland), Angles (from southern Denmark) and Saxons (from Germany)
Saxons from Germany settle in Kent
Seven kingdoms are created across Britain
St Augustine brings Christianity to Britain from Rome and becomes Archbishop of Canterbury
Mercia becomes the Supreme Kingdom; King Offa builds a Dyke along the Welsh border
England under Danelaw (area settled by the Vikings) begins
Vikings begin their attacks on England
The Oseberg Viking longship is buried (Norway)
A Viking raid on Seville is repulsed
Rus Vikings attack Constantinople (Istanbul) for the first time
Novgorod (Russia) is founded by the Rus Viking Ulrich
Danish Vikings establish a kingdom in York
Alfred the Great becomes king of Wessex; the Danish advance is halted
Harald I gains control of Norway
Rurik establishes Kiev as the centre of the Kievan Rus' domains
Alfred divides England with the Danes under the Danelaw pact
The Vikings raid along the Mediterranean coast
The Viking chief Rollo is granted land by the Franks and founds Normandy
Viking leader Erik the Red discovers Greenland
Viking ships sail in Newfoundland waters
Æthelred II pays the first Danegeld ransom to stop Danish attacks on England
Olav I dies; Norway is ruled by the Danes
Brian Boru defeats the Norse and becomes king of Ireland
Viking explorer Thorfinn Karlsefni attempts to found a settlement in North America
The Danes conquer England; Æthelred flees to Normandy
Vikings abandon the Vinland settlement on the coast of North America
The Danes under Knut (Canute) rule England
Olav II regains Norway from the Danes
Knut (Canute), king of England and Denmark, conquers Norway
Edward the Confessor rules England with the support of the Danes
The city of Oslo is founded in Norway
Battle of Stamford Bridge: Harold Godwinson (king of England) defeats Harald Hardrada (king of Norway)
Battle of Hastings: William, Duke of Normandy, defeats the Saxon king Harold (Harold's death)
The Bayeux Tapestry is made (the Norman Conquest, "medieval propaganda?")
Opening of the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition at the British Museum
The Bayeux Tapestry is loaned by France to the British Museum (London)
Norman Conquest: the last conquest, the last successful invasion of England
English has changed enough to be classed as a "new" version (Middle English)
Origins of St George's Cross (associated with the crusades)
St George's Cross adopted by England and the city of London
St George's Day (England, not really celebrated)
Union between England and Wales: step one
Union between England and Wales, step 2: Henry VIII passes the Act of Union
Welsh Language Act: separate Welsh identity restored
St David's Day (patron saint of Wales)
St Andrew's Day (patron saint of Scotland)
James VI of Scotland becomes James I of England (Elizabeth I dies without an heir)
Act of Union: English and Scottish parliaments merge = birth of Great Britain
St Patrick's Day (patron saint of Ireland)
Act of Union: Dublin parliament merges with Westminster = United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
Partition of Ireland: Irish Free State created; the six north-eastern counties (Ulster) stay in the UK
Assembly at Stormont Castle in Belfast (Northern Ireland)
Creation of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (= the UK)
The Union Jack is amended to include the cross of St Patrick (Ireland)
